what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 3: Is the static law a mixture of formation laws once the order may depend on the values?. Blocks 14, 16 (PRs #8148, #8150): on any window with a cycle the static (Gibbs) law is NOT a mixture of formation laws over value-BLIND orders (flip lemma + mixture theorem), and on the plaquette no covariant rate law, value-dependent included, gives the static law. Open beyond the plaquette: value-DEPENDENT order laws. TASK: decide it exactly on the next windows (2x3 rectangle, the cube) for the six-axis rule at a few rational weights, e.g. (p,q,r) = (3,1,2), (5,2,4), (7,3,5): is the static law in the convex hull of the laws generated by all adapted sequential formation schemes (the next site may depend on the records so far)? This is a finite linear program over the rationals: the extreme points are deterministic adapted site-selection strategies; use LP duality to produce either the mixture or an exact separating functional. A separating functional that works for every weight would be a theorem; state it. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/static-law-in-the-hull/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/static-law-in-the-hull/<name>/check.py"
